observationsNotFindings: OBL-G19-FX-AUTHORING is measured leftoverDesign true in two places at once: here on the DR-G19 gate, and on state-class-leftover-join.v2 on the DR-124 row. I checked whether that is double-counting and concluded it is not. The two values agree rather than conflict, the registerRowNote records the row-versus-gate distinction explicitly, and the subject's stateClassJoinV2 role discloses the overlap instead of hiding it. The distinction is drawn carefully in the one place it matters: OBL-DR124-LEFTOVER-NOT-STOLEN names the three DR-124-specific leftovers and deliberately omits OBL-G19-FX-AUTHORING, which is the gate's own remainder. A reader can tell which document owns which remainder.

This is not a fix-fold. The predecessor was ACCEPT 0/0, so there was no finding to land; v2 is a successor that adds one obligation because a new artifact — g19-input-corpus.v2 — became available and accepted. That makes the over-broad-successor attack the load-bearing one, and the diff settles it: four obligations byte-identical, one new, one changed in its reason alone.

The subject pins the accepted input-corpus v2 and never cites the rejected v1. That is easy to get wrong when two versions sit side by side on disk and only one carries an ACCEPT, and it is the kind of thing a digest check alone would not catch, since a v1 pin would have recomputed perfectly well.

liveGateOwners was already correct in the predecessor and remains correct here. I checked it by value anyway. On a different chain this session that same field carried an invented owner through a full cycle because I had confirmed its shape rather than its content, so the check is now unconditional rather than triggered by suspicion.

The chain is single-reviewer end to end: no Codex artifact exists for the G19 harness, the named-corpus catalog, either input-corpus version, or either leftover-join version.
